summary: Steel fire tower in Cass Scenic Railroad State Park, Pocahontas County, WV; staffed until 1977; cabin rentable since 2021; tower repair under way in 2021, later condition unknown.

facts.design: Steel tower with a metal cab
facts.status_note: Repairs were under way in 2021; no later source confirms the tower's condition.

access.note: Cass Scenic Railroad excursion trains stop at the Bald Knob overlook; the Wilderness Cabin can be booked for overnight stays.

visit.trail_note: Trains pause about 20 minutes at the overlook. A railroad history page says the overlook is not the summit, where it says an old fire tower was abandoned.

events.note: A 53-foot Blaw-Knox steel tower erected, per the Forest Lookouts page; not clearly the tower standing today
February 1930 newspaper calls it the new steel fire tower; the Register gives the early 1930s
Staff from the Paddy's Knob tower manned it in April 1958 when snow blocked the road
Last year the lookout was staffed
Wilderness Cabin open for booking by June 2021; tower still under construction

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register names the WV Division of Forestry as administrator, with the Division of Parks and Recreation as cooperator. A 2021 article says Cass Scenic Railroad State Park took possession of the tower and cabin. Both may be true; the sources do not settle who owns the tower.

The Register gives 47 feet (about 14.3 m); the Forest Lookouts page gives 53 feet (16.2 m) for the 1923 Blaw-Knox tower. The record's 16.2 m matches the 53-foot figure. Left out of facts because the sources conflict.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on the build date (Register: early 1930s; Forest Lookouts: a 1923 53-foot Blaw-Knox tower and a February 1930 'new steel fire tower') and on height (47 vs 53 feet). The story says so and does not pick one. Unresolved: whether the 1923 structure is the tower standing today. Current condition is unknown: the 2021 article says a contractor was to start repairs that summer, and the HawkinsRails page is undated and says the summit tower was abandoned; neither is a current report. The Register's visit and access details are not in the record. The cabin rental is supported only by the June 2021 article; check current booking before publishing. The record has no built year; none is proposed as a correction. No corrections proposed. Not verified on site.
